questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Symbiotic association between fungi and algae are called __________.
questions.solution:
Lichens are a mutually beneficial symbiotic association between algae (phycobiont) and fungi (mycobiont).

The algal component prepares food for fungi, and fungi provide shelter and absorb mineral nutrients and water for its partner.

Mycorrhiza is a symbiotic association between fungi and the roots of higher plants.

Chrysophytes are a group of protists that includes diatoms and golden algae.

Sponges are multicellular animals belonging to the phylum Porifera.

Answer: lichens

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q:
The main criteria used for Five Kingdom Classification proposed by R.H. Whittaker (1969) included :
A. Cell structure
B. Body organization
C. Presence of flagellum
D. Reproduction
E. Phylogenetic relationships
Choose the correct answer from the options given below :
options: A, B, C, D and E
A, B, D and E only
questions.solution:
R.H. Whittaker (1969) proposed the Five Kingdom Classification. The main criteria used by him for this classification include:
1. Cell structure (prokaryotic or eukaryotic)
2. Body organisation (unicellular or multicellular)
3. Mode of nutrition (autotrophic or heterotrophic)
4. Reproduction
5. Phylogenetic relationships

Presence of flagellum was not used as a main criterion for the Five Kingdom Classification.

Therefore, the correct criteria from the given list are A, B, D, and E.

Answer: A, B, D and E only

Each of the following characteristics represent a Kingdom proposed by Whittaker. Arrange the following in increasing order of complexity of body organization.
A. Multicellular heterotrophs with cell wall made of chitin.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Mad cow disease is caused by __________.
questions.solution:
Mad cow disease, scientifically known as Bovine Spongiform Encephalopathy (BSE), is a fatal neurodegenerative disease in cattle.

It is caused by prions, which are abnormally folded infectious proteins. Prions induce abnormal folding of specific normal cellular proteins found most abundantly in the brain, leading to brain damage and the characteristic signs of the disease.

Viroids are infectious RNA molecules that cause plant diseases, Mycoplasma are bacteria lacking a cell wall, and Aspergillus is a fungus.

Answer: prions

questions.solution:
The ascomycetes are commonly known as sac-fungi. They are mostly multicellular, e.g., Penicillium, or rarely unicellular, e.g., yeast (Saccharomyces).

Statement $I$: Mycoplasma can pass through less than 1 micron filter size.

Statement $II$: Mycoplasma are bacteria with cell wall.

options: Both Statement $I$ and Statement $II$ are incorrect
Statement $I$ is correct but Statement $II$ is incorrect
Statement $I$ is incorrect but Statement $II$ is correct
Both Statement $I$ and Statement $II$ are correct
questions.solution:
Statement $I$: Mycoplasma can pass through even $0 . 22$ micron filters which are smaller than $1$ micron.

So, the statement $I$ is correct.

Statement $II$: Mycoplasma is a pleomorphic bacterium without a cell wall and hence it can easily change its shape, due to which it can pass through the filters easily.

So, statement $II$ is incorrect.

questions.solution:
Diatoms are chief producers in the oceans, and they contribute to 40% of the ocean's primary productivity. They constitute a major group of unicellular eukaryotic microscopic algae and are among the most common types of phytoplanktons found floating on the surface of the seas.

Fungi are eukaryotic organisms, meaning they possess a well-defined nucleus and membrane-bound organelles. Therefore, fungi are not prokaryotes.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Viroids differ from viruses in having:
questions.solution:
Viroids are sub-viral agents as infectious RNA particles, without a protein coat.

Virus:- It is a small infectious agent that replicates only inside the living cells of other organisms. It is an obligate intracellular parasite which can reproduce only by invading and taking over other cells as they lack the cellular machinery for self-reproduction.

Viroids:- These are the smallest infectious pathogens known. These are subviral, smallest known agents of infectious disease. The term viroid was coined by T.O. Diener (1971) to describe the agent of the potato spindle tuber disease. There are some 25 viroids which vary in nucleotide sequence. These are spread by plant propagation through seeds and by manual mishandling with contaminated implements.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Mycorrhizae are the example of:
questions.solution: Mycorrhizae are symbiotic relationships that form between fungi and plants. The fungi colonize the root system of a host plant, providing increased water and nutrient absorption capabilities while the plant provides the fungus with carbohydrates formed from photosynthesis. Mycorrhizal fungi encompass many major groups of the fungus Kingdom and in the past were divided into two non-evolutionarily related groups: the ectotrophic and endotrophic based upon the position of the fungal hyphae in relation to the tissues of a plants roots. Ectomycorrhizal fungi ensheath the root cells but usually do not penetrate them (extracellular). Endomycorrhizal fungi penetrate and enter the cells of a plant root

questions.q: Methanogens belong to:
questions.solution:
ARCHAEBACTERIA:

These archaebacteria are special since they live in some of the harshest habitats such as extreme salty areas (halophiles), hot springs (thermoacidophiles), and marshy areas (methanogens).
Archaebacteria differ from other bacteria in having a different cell wall structure and this feature is responsible for their survival in extreme conditions.

Archaebacteria are divided into three groups - methanogens, halophiles, and thermoacidophiles.

Methanogens: These bacteria are of marshy habitats. They are capable of converting CO2, methanol, and formic acid into methane so named methanogens. These methanogens are present in the guts of several ruminant animals such as cows and buffaloes, and they are responsible for the production of methane (biogas) from the dung of these animals. These are chemoautotrophs.
Examples: Methanococcus, Methanobacterium, etc.

questions.solution:
Viroids are smaller than viruses, self–replicating particles that were discovered by T.O. Diener (1971). Viroids are infectious RNA particles that are devoid of protein coat. The molecular weight of RNA in viroid is low in comparison to viruses. Potato spindle tuber is a viroid causing disease.

DISCOVERIES OF VIROLOGY:

  • Term virus (means venom or poisonous fluid) was coined by Pasteur (1880).
  • D.J. Ivanowsky (1892) recognized certain microbes as causal organisms of the mosaic disease of tobacco. These were found to be smaller than bacteria because they passed through bacteria-proof filters.
  • M.W. Beijerinek (1898) demonstrated that the extract of the infected plants of tobacco could cause infection in healthy plants and called this fluid as Contagium vivum fluidum (infectious living fluid).
  • W.M. Stanley (1935) crystallized TMV (Tobacco mosaic virus) for the first time. He showed that viruses could be crystallized and crystals consist largely of proteins.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: The term 'glycocalyx' is used for:
options: a layer present bet ween cell wall and membrane of bacteria
bacterial cell glyco-engineered to possess $\mathrm{N}$-glycosylated proteins
a layer surrounding the cell wall of bacteria
questions.solution:
Glycocalyx is a gelatinous polysaccharide and/or polypeptide covering present in the cell envelop in bacteria. When it occurs in the form of a loose sheath, it is known as a slime layer. When it occurs in the form of a thick and tough mucilage covering, it is called a capsule. Glycocalyx assists cells in adhesion to a solid surface, and also protects pathogenic bacteria from the attack of the host's immune system. It provides protection against desiccation and holds the bacterial cells together.
Related Theory
The animal cells and protists have an external covering over their plasma membrane which is known as a cell coat or glycocalyx and it found in bacteria. Unlike cell wall that is made up of cellulose, the cell coat is made up of a filamentous layer of oligosaccharide and glycoprotein. This layer is usually a part of the cell membrane and provides biochemical identity on the cell surface. The cell coat is strengthened and supported by the deposition of calcium salts, silicon and other materials.

questions.solution: Prions have a distinct extracellular form but the extracellular form is entirely protein. The prion particle does not contain any nucleic acid. However, it is infectious and prions are known to cause a variety of diseases in animals such as scrapie in sheep, bovine spongiform encephalopathy in cattle (BSE or 'mad cow disease'), chronic wasting disease in deer and elk and Kuru and a form of Creutzfeldt-Jakob disease (CJD) in humans. No prion diseases of plants are known.

Archaea have some novel features that are absent in other prokaryotes and eukaryotes
Archaea completely differ from both prokaryotes and eukaryotes
questions.solution:
The term archaebacteria refers to the ancient origin of this group of bacteria, which seems to have diverged very early from the eubacteria. All archaebacteria share certain key characteristics.
(i) Their cell wall lack peptidoglycan (important component of cell wall of eubacteria).
(ii) Lipids in cell membrane of archaebacteria have different structure than those in all other organisms.
(iii) Archaebacteria have distinct ribosomal RNA sequence.
(iv) Some genes of archaebacteria possess introns unlike those of other bacteria.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Which one of the following statements is correct?
options: Both Azotobacter and Rhizobium fix atmospheric nitrogen in root nodules of plants.
Cyanobacteria such as Anabaena and Nostoc are important mobilizers of phosphates and for plant nutrition in soil
At present it is not possible to grow maize without chemical fertilizers
Extensive use of chemical fertilizers may lead to eutrophication of nearby water bodies.
questions.solution:
Rhizobium fix nitrogen in root nodules of legumes, while Azotobacter is a free-living nitrogen-fixing bacterium. Anabaena and Nostoc are not mobilisers of phosphates. Anabaena is a filamentous cyanobacteria, involved in nitrogen fixation. Extensive use of chemical fertilizers may lead to eutrophication of nearby waterbodies.
Related Theory
Eutrophication or more precisely hypertrophication, refers to enrichment of $a$ water body with nutrients, usually with an excess amount of nutrients. This process induces growth of plants and algae and, due to the biomass load, may result in oxygen depletion of the water body. For example, algal bloom.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: A genetically engineered micro-organism used successfully in bioremediation of oil spills is a species of:
questions.solution:
A genetically engineered microorganism called Pseudomonas putida is used in thebioremediation of oil spills. It is also known as super bug and was discovered by Ananda Mohan Chakrabarty. Cyclosporin is obtained from Trichoderma polysporum which is used as immunosuppressive agent. Xanthomonas is a disease causing gram negative bacteria.
Related Theory
Bioremediation is a biotechnical process which involves the removal of complex material or contamination by degrading environmental pollutants using living microorganisms. The ability of micro-organisms could be enhanced by providing optimum growth conditions to micro-organism or by employing the genetically modified microorganisms (GMMs). This technology has been implemented to eradicate environmentally hazardous chemicals and detoxify them into nontoxic forms.
Caution
Bioaugmentation involves the injection of a small amount of oil-degrading microbes into an affected area. Biostimulation is the addition of nutrients to stimulate the growth of innate oil-degrading microbes to increase the rate of remediation.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: The thalloid body of a slime mould (myxomycetes) is known as:
questions.solution:
The thalloid body of Myxomycetes is called plasmodium. It is a multinucleate diploid body which propagates through fission or thickwalled cysts or sclerotium-like structures. Fruiting bodies and mycelium are absent in lower fungi. Protenoma is not formed in fungi, but in bryophytes (sporophyte).
Related Theory
The members of Myxomycetes are called slime moulds because they contain and secrete slime. They are included in lower fungi. Their somatic phase is a multinucleate, diploid holocarpic Plasmodium (a product of syngamy). Reproduction takes place by the formation of uninucleate, thick-walled resting spores which are produced within minute fruiting bodies like structures i.e., the sporangia, however, the true fruiting bodies are absent in slime moulds.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Which one of the following statements about mycoplasma is wrong?
questions.solution:
Characteristics of Mycoplasma:
(i) Cell wall is absent and plasma membrane forms the outer boundary of the cell.
(ii) Due to the absence of cell wall these organisms can change their shape and are pleomorphic and are inherently resistant to lactam antibiotics (e.g., penicillin).
(iii) Lack of nucleus and other membranebound organelles. Genetic material is a single DNA duplex and is naked. Ribosomes are $70 \mathrm{~S}$ type.
(iv) Shows Heterotrophic nutrition. (Saprophytes and parasitic). M. pneumoniae causes lung infections such as walking pneumonia.
(v) They are found in the pleural cavities of cattle suffering from pleuropneumonia. These organisms are often called PPLO (pleuropneumonia-like organisms).
Related Theory
In the treatment of mycoplasmal pneumonia, antimicrobials against $M$ pneumoniae are bacteriostatic, not bactericidal. Tetracycline and erythromycin compounds are very effective as they are protein synthesis inhibitors.

questions.q:
Which of the following environmental conditions are essential for optimum growth of Mucor on a piece of bread?
(I) Temperature of about $25^{\circ} \mathrm{C}$
(II) Temperature of about $5^{\circ} \mathrm{C}$
(III) Relative humidity of about $5 \%$
(IV) Relative humidity of about $95 \%$
(V) A shady place
(VI) A brightly illuminated place
Choose the answer from the following options.
questions.solution:
Mucor is a saprophytic fungus. It grows on decaying dung and on some food stuffs. It shows the best growth on a piece of bread at about $25^{\circ} \mathrm{C}$ with relative humidity of about $95 \%$ in moist and shady places.
Related Theory
Mucor is a genus of mould. They are formed from thread-like hyphae that spread out from a visible mycelium. It causes mucormycosis. Most people develop this infection by breathing in mould spores. Less often, infection can develop when spores enter the body through a cut or open wound. It was much prevalent during second wave of COVID-19 (as black fungus) in 2021 in India.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: What is common about Trypanosoma. Noctiluca, Monocystis and Giardia?
questions.solution: Trypanosoma gambiense is the single celled, parasitic zoofiagellate causing trypanosomiasis or sleeping sickness. Giardia is a parasitic flagellate occurring in the intestine of man and other animals and causes giardiasis or diarrhoea (i.e., very loose and frequent stool containing large quantity of fat). Noctiluca is a marine, colourless dinoflagellate. It is a voracious predator and has a long, motile tentacle, near the base of which, its single short flagellum emerges. Monocystis is a microscopic, unicellular endoparasitic protozoan found in the coelom and seminal vesicles of earthworm. As it is an endoparasite, it does not possess any special structure for locomotion.

questions.q: T O Diener discovered a
questions.solution: Viroids are small, circular, single stranded RNA molecules that are the smallest known pathogens. The extracellular form of the viroid is naked RNA, ie, there is no protein capsid of any kind. Even, the RNA molecule contains no protein encoding genes and therefore, the viroid is totally dependent on host function for its replication. No viroid diseases of animals are known and the precise mechanisms by which viroids cause plant diseases remain unclear.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Some hyperthermophilic organisms that grow in highly acidic ( $\mathrm{pH} 2$ ) habitats belong to the two groups called
questions.solution: Thermophiles live in very hot places, typically from $60^{\circ}$ to $80^{\circ} \mathrm{C}$. Many thermophiles (some eubacteria and archaebacteria) are autotrophs and have metabolisms based on sulphur. Some thermophilic archaebacteria form the basis of food webs around deep-sea thermal vents, where they must withstand extreme temperature and pressures. Archaebacteria can grow in highly acidic $(\mathrm{pH}=0.7)$ and very basic $(\mathrm{pH}=11)$ environments.

Prions are the infectious agents responsible for several neurodegenerative diseases in mammals. This happens due to the abnormal folding of the proteins in the brain. They can break down the nucleic acids, but are receptive to substances that denature proteins.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: In bacteria, plasmid is:
questions.solution:
A plasmid is a small, often circular DNA molecule found in bacteria and other cells. Plasmids are separate from the bacterial chromosome and replicate independently of it.
Related Theory
Each bacterial cell typically produces many copies of a plasmid, in contrast to making only one copy of its own chromosome. The fact that plasmids are smaller and in greater number than the host chromosome make plasmids easier to isolate in pure form, which is why researchers commonly use them for studying DNA in the laboratory. Plasmids are thus a fundamental tool of recombinant DNA technology.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: The chief advantage of encystment of an Amoeba is:
options: the ability to survive during adverse physical conditions
the ability to live for some time without ingesting food
the chance to get rid of accumulated waste products
questions.solution:
During adverse environmental periods, Amoeba survive by encystment by becoming circular, loses most of its water, and secretes a cyst membrane that serves as a protective covering. When the environment is again suitable, the envelope ruptures and the Amoeba emerges.
Related Theory
During unfavourable conditions, Amoeba undergo multiple fission inside the cyst to survive and reproduce under unfavourable conditions. In the multiplefission, the nucleus of the parent cell divides multiple times by amitosis (direct cell division), producing several nuclei. The cytoplasm, later on, separates, creating multiple daughter cells. When the conditions are unfavourable, Amoeba withdraws its pseudopodia and becomes almost round.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Viruses are no more "alive" than isolated chromosomes because:
options: they require both RNA and DNA
they both require oxygen for respiration
both require the environment of a cell to replicate
questions.solution:
Outside of a host cell, viruses do not use any energy. They only become active when they come into contact with a host cell. Once activated, they use the host cell's energy and tools to make more viruses. Because they do not use their own energy, some scientists do not consider them alive.
Related Theory
The only point favouring the virus as living entities is that they have the ability to reproduce (multiply) within the host by using host's machinery. The only point favouring the viruses as living entities is that they have the ability to reproduce (multiply)-though in the host using host's machinery.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Which one of the following statements about viruses is correct?
options: viruses possess their own metabolic system
all viruses contain both RNA and DNA
nucleic acid of viruses is known as capsid
questions.solution:
Viruses consist of a protein coat known as capsid which encloses a single type of nucleic acid, either RNA or DNA. They do not have enzymes for protein synthesis. They require living host cell for multiplication, while they take over the machinery of the host cell. Thus, viruses are obligatory intercellular parasites.
Related Theory
Viruses can infect all cellular life forms, but each cellular species can be infected by own limited specific range of viruses. Most viruses that harm animals can not harm humans.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Which Kingdom does Protista Kingdom form a link with?
questions.solution: All single-celled eukaryotes are placed under Protista, but the boundaries of this kingdom are not well defined. What may be ‘a photosynthetic protistan’ to one biologist may be ‘a plant’ to another. In this book we include Chrysophytes, Dinoflagellates, Euglenoids, Slime moulds and Protozoans under Protista. Members of Protista are primarily aquatic. <mark style="background-color: yellow, turquious;"> This kingdom forms a link with the others dealing with plants, animals and fungi. </mark>  Being eukaryotes, the protistan cell body contains a well defined nucleus and other membrane-bound organelles. Some have flagella or cilia. Protists reproduce asexually and sexually by a process involvingcell fusion and zygote formation.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: In which environments are chrysophytes typically found?
options: Both fresh water and marine environments
questions.solution: This group includes diatoms and golden algae (desmids). <mark style="background-color: yellow, turquious;"> They are found in fresh water as well as in marine environments. </mark> They are microscopic and float passively in water currents (plankton). Most of them are photosynthetic. In diatoms the cell walls form two thin overlapping shells, which fit together as in a soap box. The walls are embedded with silica and thus the walls are indestructible. Thus, diatoms have left behind large amount of cell wall deposits in their habitat; this accumulation over billions of years is referred to as ‘diatomaceous earth’. Being gritty this soil is used in polishing, filtration of oils and syrups. Diatoms are the chief ‘producers’ in the oceans.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: What is the main characteristic of dinoflagellates?
options: They are mostly marine and photosynthetic
questions.solution: <mark style="background-color: yellow, turquious;"> These organisms are mostly marine and photosynthetic. </mark> They appear yellow, green, brown, blue or red depending on the main pigments present in their cells. The cell wallhas stiff cellulose plates on the outer surface. Most of them have two flagella; one lies longitudinally and the other transversely in a furrow between the wall plates. Very often, red dinoflagellates (Example: Gonyaulax) undergo such rapid multiplication that they make the sea appear red (red tides). Toxins released by such large numbers may even kill other marine animals such as fishes.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: In which type of environment are the majority of euglenoids found?
questions.solution: <mark style="background-color: yellow, turquious;">  Majority of them are fresh water organisms found in stagnant water. </mark>  Instead of a cell wall, they have a protein rich layer called pellicle which makes their body flexible. They have two flagella, a short and a long one. Though they are photosynthetic in the presence of sunlight, when deprived of sunlight they behave like heterotrophs by predating on other smaller organisms. Interestingly, the pigments of euglenoids are identical to those present in higher plants. Example: Euglena

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: What is the name of the aggregation formed by slime moulds under suitable conditions?
questions.solution: Slime moulds are saprophytic protists. The body moves along decaying twigs and leaves engulfing organic material. <mark style="background-color: yellow, turquious;"> Under suitable conditions, they form an aggregation called plasmodium which may grow and spread over several feet. </mark>  During unfavourable conditions, the plasmodium differentiates and forms fruiting bodies bearing spores at their tips. The spores possess true walls. They are extremely resistant and survive for many years, even under adverse conditions. The spores are dispersed by air currents.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: What is the Kingdom of fungi classified as?
questions.solution: <mark style="background-color: yellow, turquious;">  The fungi constitute a unique kingdom of heterotrophic organisms. </mark> They show a great diversity in morphology and habitat. You must have seen fungi on a moist bread and rotten fruits. The common mushroom you eat and toadstools are also fungi. White spots seen on mustard leaves are due to a parasitic fungus. Some unicellular fungi, e.g., yeast are used to make bread and beer. Other fungi cause diseases in plants and animals; wheat rust-causing Puccinia is an important example. Some are the source of antibiotics, e.g., Penicillium.

questions.solution: <mark style="background-color: yellow, turquious;"> With the exception of yeasts which are unicellular, </mark>  fungi are filamentous. Their bodies consist of long, slender thread-like structures called hyphae. The network of hyphae is known as mycelium. Some hyphae are continuous tubes filled with multinucleated cytoplasm – these are called coenocytic hyphae. Others have septae or cross walls in their hyphae. The cell walls of fungi are composed of chitin and polysaccharides.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: What is the role of fungi in causing disease?
options: They are responsible for causing diseases in plants and animals
They are the source of antibiotics
They prevent food from going bad
They cause white spots on mustard leaves
questions.solution: The common mushroom you eat and toadstools are also fungi. White spots seen on mustard leaves are due to a parasitic fungus. Some unicellular fungi, e.g., yeast are used to make bread and beer. <mark style="background-color: yellow, turquious;"> Other fungi cause diseases in plants and animals; wheat rust-causing Puccinia is an important example. </mark> Some are the source of antibiotics, e.g., Penicillium.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: What happens when two haploid hyphae of compatible mating types come together in case of Aspergillus , Claviceps and Neurospora?
questions.solution: When a fungus reproduces sexually, <mark style="background-color: yellow, turquious;">  two haploid hyphae of compatible mating types come together and fuse. In some fungi the fusion of two haploid cells immediately results in diploid cells (2n). However, in other fungi (ascomycetes and basidiomycetes), an interveningdikaryotic stage (n + n, i.e., two nuclei per cell) occurs; such a condition is called a dikaryon and the phase is called dikaryophase of fungus. </mark>  Later, the parental nuclei fuse and the cells become diploid. The fungi form fruiting bodies in which reduction division occurs, leading to formation of haploid spores.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Where can members of phycomycetes be found?
options: Decaying wood in moist and damp places
questions.solution: <mark style="background-color: yellow, turquious;">  Members of phycomycetes are found in aquatic habitats and on decaying wood in moist and damp places or as obligate parasites on plants. </mark> The mycelium is aseptate and coenocytic. Asexual reproduction takes place by zoospores (motile) or by aplanospores (non-motile). These spores are endogenously produced in sporangium. A zygospore is formed by fusion of two gametes. These gametes are similar in morphology (isogamous) or dissimilar (anisogamous or oogamous). Some common examples are Mucor, Rhizopus (the breadmould mentioned earlier) and Albugo (the parasitic fungi on mustard).

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: What are the common forms of basidiomycetes?
questions.solution: <mark style="background-color: yellow, turquious;"> Commonly known forms of basidiomycetes are mushrooms, bracket fungi or puffballs. </mark> They grow in soil, on logs and tree stumps and in living plant bodies as parasites, e.g., rusts and smuts. The mycelium is branched and septate. The asexual spores are generally not found, but vegetative reproduction by fragmentation is common. The sex organs are absent,but plasmogamy is brought about by fusion of two vegetative or somatic cells of different strains or genotypes. The resultant structure is dikaryotic which ultimately gives rise to basidium. Karyogamy and meiosis take place in the basidium producing four basidiospores. The basidiospores are exogenously produced on the basidium (pl.: basidia). The basidia are arranged in fruiting bodies called basidiocarps. Some common members are Agaricus (mushroom), Ustilago (smut) and Puccinia (rust fungus).

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: What are deuteromycetes commonly known as?
questions.solution: <mark style="background-color: yellow, turquious;"> Commonly known as imperfect fungi</mark>  because only the asexual or vegetative phases of these fungi are known. When the sexual forms of these fungi were discovered they were moved into classes they rightly belong to. It is also possible that the asexual and vegetative stage have been given one name (and placed under deuteromycetes) and the sexualstage another (and placed under another class). Later when the linkages were established, the fungi were correctly identified and moved out of deuteromycetes. Once perfect (sexual) stages of members of dueteromycetes were discovered they were often moved to ascomycetesand basidiomycetes. The deuteromycetes reproduce only by asexual spores known as conidia. The mycelium is septate and branched. Some members are saprophytes or parasites while a large number of them are decomposers of litter and help in mineral cycling. Some examples areAlternaria, Colletotrichum and Trichoderma.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Who recognized certain microbes as the causal organism of the mosaic disease of tobacco?
questions.solution: Virus means venom or poisonous fluid. <mark style="background-color: yellow, turquious;"> Dmitri Ivanowsky (1892) recognised certain microbes as causal organism of the mosaic disease of tobacco. </mark> These were found to be smaller than bacteria because they passed through bacteria-proof filters. M.W. Beijerinek(1898) demonstrated that the extract of the infected plants of tobacco could cause infection in healthy plants and named the new pathogen “virus” and called the fluid as Contagium vivum fluidum (infectious living fluid). W.M. Stanley (1935) showed that viruses could be crystallisedand crystals consist largely of proteins. They are inert outside their specific host cell. Viruses are obligate parasites.

Dmitri Ivanowsky (1892) recognised certain microbes as causal organism of the mosaic disease of tobacco. <mark style="background-color: yellow, turquious;"> These were found to be smaller than bacteria because they passed through bacteria-proof filters. </mark>  M.W. Beijerinek(1898) demonstrated that the extract of the infected plants of tobacco could cause infection in healthy plants and named the new pathogen “virus” and called the fluid as Contagium vivum fluidum (infectious living fluid). questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: What are the types of genetic material found in viruses?
questions.solution: In addition to proteins, <mark style="background-color: yellow, turquious;"> viruses also contain genetic material, that could be either RNA or DNA. </mark>  No virus contains both RNA and DNA. A virus is a nucleoprotein and the genetic material is infectious. In general, viruses that infect plants have single stranded RNA and viruses that infect animals have either single or double stranded RNA or double stranded DNA.Bacterial viruses or bacteriophages (viruses that infect the bacteria) are usually double stranded DNA viruses. The protein coat called capsid made of small subunits called capsomeres, protects the nucleic acid. These capsomeres are arranged in helical or polyhedralgeometric forms. Viruses cause diseases like mumps, small pox, herpes and influenza. AIDS in humans is also caused by a virus. In plants, the symptoms can be mosaic formation, leaf rolling and curling, yellowing and vein clearing, dwarfing and stunted growth.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: What is the algal component of lichens known as?
questions.solution: Lichens are symbiotic associations i.e. mutually useful associations, between algae and fungi. <mark style="background-color: yellow, turquious;"> The algal component is known as phycobiont</mark>  and fungal component as mycobiont, which are autotrophic and heterotrophic, respectively. Algae prepare food for fungi and fungi provide shelter and absorb mineral nutrients and water for its partner. So close is their association that if one saw a lichen in nature one would never imagine that they had two different organisms within them. Lichens are very good pollution indicators – they do not grow in polluted areas.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Who first proposed the Biological Classification of plants and animals?
questions.solution: <mark style="background-color: yellow, turquious;"> Biological classification of plants and animals was first proposed by Aristotle</mark>  on the basis of simple morphological characters. Linnaeus later classified all living organismsinto two kingdoms – Plantae and Animalia. Whittaker proposed an elaborate five kingdom classification – Monera, Protista, Fungi, Plantae and Animalia. The main criteria of the five kingdom classification were cell structure, body organisation, mode of nutrition and reproduction, and phylogenetic relationships.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q:
DescriptionKingdom
A. Unicellular, eukaryotic organisms1. Kingdom Monera
B. Prokaryotic, non-cellulosic cell wall2. Kingdom Plantae
C. Eukaryotic, multicellular with chitin in cell walls3. Kingdom Animalia
D. Heterotrophic with holozoic nutrition4. Kingdom Fungi
E. Eukaryotic, autotrophic with tissue and organ system5. Kingdom Protista
questions.solution:
A - 5: Unicellular, eukaryotic organisms are placed in Kingdom Protista. Protists are eukaryotes and primarily unicellular, including organisms such as algae and protozoa.
B - 1: Prokaryotic organisms with non-cellulosic cell walls are categorized under Kingdom Monera. Monerans include bacteria, which have a cell wall made up of peptidoglycan (not cellulose).
C - 4: Eukaryotic, multicellular organisms with chitin in their cell walls belong to Kingdom Fungi. Fungi have chitin in their cell walls and are primarily decomposers or parasites.
D - 3: Organisms that are heterotrophic with holozoic nutrition fall under Kingdom Animalia. Animals ingest organic matter and digest it internally, which is typical of holozoic nutrition.
E - 2: Eukaryotic organisms that are autotrophic and have tissue and organ systems are placed in Kingdom Plantae. Plants are multicellular, have chloroplasts for photosynthesis, and have organized tissues and organs.

questions.q:
Type of Bacteria/CharacteristicDescription
A. Eubacteria1. Smallest living cells, lack a cell wall
B. Cyanobacteria2. Rigid cell wall, can be motile with a flagellum
C. Mycoplasma3. Photosynthetic autotrophs, can fix atmospheric nitrogen
D. Heterotrophic bacteria4. Decomposers, involved in nitrogen fixation, some are pathogens
questions.solution:

D - 4: Heterotrophic bacteria are the most abundant bacteria in nature, primarily functioning as decomposers. They are involved in processes such as nitrogen fixation (in the roots of legumes), and some species are pathogenic, causing diseases like cholera, typhoid, tetanus, and citrus canker.

D - 2: Slime Moulds are saprophytic protists that form a plasmodium during their life cycle. They produce spores that are resistant and can survive adverse conditions.

questions.q:
In a particular group of fungi, asexual spores are produced exogenously on special mycelia, while sexual spores are produced endogenously in sac-like structures.

Identify the fungal class and its correct set of examples.
questions.solution:
The description states that asexual spores are produced exogenously (conidia on conidiophores) and sexual spores are produced endogenously in sac-like structures (ascospores in asci). These are the defining features of the class Ascomycetes (sac fungi).

Aspergillus, Claviceps, and Neurospora are all correct examples of Ascomycetes.

Basidiomycetes typically lack asexual spores and produce sexual spores exogenously on basidia. Phycomycetes produce asexual spores endogenously in sporangia. Alternaria and Trichoderma belong to Deuteromycetes, making the fourth option incorrect despite correctly naming the class.

Answer: Ascomycetes; Aspergillus, Claviceps, Neurospora

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q:
An unknown organism is discovered. Preliminary analysis shows that it has a eukaryotic cell structure and a tissue level of body organisation.

To definitively classify this organism into one of the five kingdoms proposed by R.H. Whittaker, which pair of additional characteristics MUST be ascertained?
options: Presence of a nuclear membrane and mode of reproduction
Cell wall composition and mode of nutrition
questions.solution:
The organism is eukaryotic and has a tissue level of body organisation. According to Whittaker's five-kingdom classification, organisms with eukaryotic cells and tissue-level (or higher) organisation can belong to Kingdom Fungi (multicellular/loose tissue), Kingdom Plantae (tissue/organ), or Kingdom Animalia (tissue/organ/organ system).

To distinguish among these three kingdoms, one must determine the mode of nutrition and the nature of the cell wall. Fungi are heterotrophic with a chitinous cell wall, Plantae are autotrophic with a cellulosic cell wall, and Animalia are heterotrophic without a cell wall.

The presence of a nuclear membrane and cell type are already established by the fact that the organism is eukaryotic. Therefore, ascertaining the cell wall composition and mode of nutrition is essential and sufficient for definitive classification.

Answer: Cell wall composition and mode of nutrition

Phylogenetic relationships and mode of reproduction
Cell structure and mode of nutrition

Assertion (A): The size of PPLO is about $0.1\ \mu\text{m}$, whereas typical eukaryotic cells are $10-20\ \mu\text{m}$ in size.
Reason (R): Prokaryotic organisms like PPLO generally multiply more rapidly than typical eukaryotic cells.

In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
options: Both Assertion and Reason are true and Reason is the correct explanation of Assertion.
Both Assertion and Reason are true but Reason is not the correct explanation of Assertion.
Assertion is true but Reason is false.
Assertion is false but Reason is true.
questions.solution:
Both Assertion and Reason are true statements according to NCERT.

The size of PPLO is about $0.1\ \mu\text{m}$, and typical eukaryotic cells are $10-20\ \mu\text{m}$ in size. This makes the Assertion true.

Prokaryotic cells (including PPLO) are generally smaller and multiply more rapidly than eukaryotic cells. This makes the Reason true.

However, the rapid multiplication of PPLO (Reason) is not the cause of their small size (Assertion). In biological terms, it is their smaller size and simpler organization that allows them to multiply more rapidly, not the other way around. Therefore, the Reason is not the correct explanation for the Assertion.

Answer: Both Assertion and Reason are true but Reason is not the correct explanation of Assertion.

Assertion (A): In Whittaker's Five Kingdom classification, Chlamydomonas and Amoeba were brought together in Kingdom Protista.

Reason (R): The shift in classification criteria to include cell structure and body organisation grouped all unicellular eukaryotes together, regardless of the presence or absence of a cell wall.

options: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of Assertion (A)

Assertion (A) is false but Reason (R) is true
questions.solution:

Whittaker's system used cell structure (prokaryotic vs eukaryotic) and body organisation (unicellular vs multicellular) as primary criteria. This change resulted in all unicellular eukaryotes being grouped together in Protista, overriding the older cell wall-based plant/animal distinction.

Therefore, both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of Assertion (A).

Answer: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of Assertion (A)

Answer: Mycoplasma

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: A biologist observes an organism forming extensive blooms in a highly polluted water body. Upon further analysis, the organism is found to be a photosynthetic autotroph possessing chlorophyll $a$ similar to green plants. Which of the following statements is true regarding this organism?
options: It belongs to Archaebacteria and possesses a different cell wall structure for survival in extreme conditions.
It is a Eubacterium and some of its members possess specialised cells called heterocysts for nitrogen fixation.
It is a chemosynthetic autotroph that oxidises various inorganic substances to recycle nutrients.
It is a methanogen that survives in aquatic environments and produces biogas.
questions.solution:
The organism described forms blooms in polluted water bodies and possesses chlorophyll $a$ similar to green plants. These features are characteristic of Cyanobacteria (blue-green algae).

Cyanobacteria belong to the group Eubacteria (true bacteria). Some members of Cyanobacteria, such as Nostoc and Anabaena, have specialised cells called heterocysts that help in fixing atmospheric nitrogen.

They are not Archaebacteria, nor are they chemosynthetic autotrophs (which oxidise inorganic substances) or methanogens (which are Archaebacteria found in marshy areas or ruminant guts).

Answer: It is a Eubacterium and some of its members possess specialised cells called heterocysts for nitrogen fixation.

Assertion (A): Cyanobacteria are placed in Kingdom Monera despite being commonly referred to as blue-green algae.
Reason (R): Cyanobacteria have chlorophyll 'a' similar to green plants but completely lack a membrane-bound nucleus and organelles.

(A) is not correct but (R) is correct
questions.solution:
Assertion (A) is correct because cyanobacteria are historically called blue-green algae due to their photosynthetic ability and appearance, yet they are taxonomically classified under Kingdom Monera.

Reason (R) is also correct and provides the exact taxonomic justification for this classification. According to the five-kingdom classification by R.H. Whittaker, the defining feature of Kingdom Monera is prokaryotic cell organization (lack of a membrane-bound nucleus and other membrane-bound organelles). Even though cyanobacteria possess plant-like chlorophyll 'a' and perform oxygenic photosynthesis, their prokaryotic cellular structure mandates their placement in Monera rather than Plantae or Protista.

Therefore, both (A) and (R) are true, and (R) correctly explains (A).

Answer: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)

questions.solution:
Organisms possessing a true nucleus are eukaryotes.

Penicillium is a fungus and belongs to the eukaryotes, hence it possesses a true, membrane-bound nucleus.

Answer: Penicillium

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q:
Read the following statements carefully:
(a) Bacteria reproduce mainly by fission.
(b) All cyanobacteria can fix atmospheric nitrogen in specialized cells called heterocysts.
(c) Chemosynthetic autotrophic bacteria oxidize various inorganic substances to produce ATP.
(d) Slime moulds form a plasmodium under unfavourable conditions.
(e) Mycoplasma are pathogenic to animals but not to plants.

How many of the above statements are correct?
questions.solution:
Let us evaluate each statement based on NCERT facts:

(a) Correct: Bacteria reproduce mainly by fission.
(b) Incorrect: Not all, but only 'some' cyanobacteria (like Nostoc and Anabaena) can fix atmospheric nitrogen in specialized cells called heterocysts.
(c) Correct: Chemosynthetic autotrophic bacteria oxidize inorganic substances (such as nitrates, nitrites, and ammonia) and use the released energy for ATP production.
(d) Incorrect: Slime moulds form an aggregation called plasmodium under 'suitable' (favourable) conditions. During unfavourable conditions, the plasmodium differentiates and forms fruiting bodies bearing spores at their tips.
(e) Incorrect: Many mycoplasma are pathogenic to both animals and plants, not just animals.

Only statements (a) and (c) are correct. Therefore, the total number of correct statements is two.

Answer: Two

questions.q:
Read the given descriptions of two organisms, X and Y:
Organism X is marine and photosynthetic, appearing yellow, green, brown, blue, or red depending on the main pigments present in its cells.
Organism Y is found in stagnant water, photosynthesises in the presence of sunlight, but predates on smaller organisms when deprived of sunlight.

Select the correct statement regarding the cell wall or outer covering of organisms X and Y.
options: X has stiff cellulose plates on the outer surface, while Y lacks a cell wall and has a protein-rich pellicle.
X has overlapping silica shells, while Y has stiff cellulose plates on the outer surface.
X lacks a cell wall and has a protein-rich pellicle, while Y has stiff cellulose plates on the outer surface.
Both X and Y possess a cellulosic cell wall, but only Y has a protein-rich pellicle.
questions.solution:
Based on the given descriptions, organism X is a dinoflagellate because they are mostly marine, photosynthetic, and appear in various colours depending on their pigments.

Organism Y is a euglenoid because they are found in stagnant water and exhibit mixotrophic nutrition (photosynthetic in light, heterotrophic in dark).

Dinoflagellates (X) have stiff cellulose plates on the outer surface of their cell wall.

Euglenoids (Y) lack a cell wall; instead, they have a protein-rich layer called a pellicle which makes their body flexible.

Therefore, the correct statement is that X has stiff cellulose plates, while Y lacks a cell wall and has a pellicle.

Answer: X has stiff cellulose plates on the outer surface, while Y lacks a cell wall and has a protein-rich pellicle.

Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R).

Assertion (A): Blue-green algae are classified under Kingdom Plantae because they perform oxygenic photosynthesis.
Reason (R): Blue-green algae are prokaryotic organisms that lack a true nucleus and membrane-bound cell organelles.

In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
options: Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).
Both (A) and (R) are true but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A).
questions.solution:
Assertion (A) is false because blue-green algae (cyanobacteria) are not classified under Kingdom Plantae. In R.H. Whittaker's five-kingdom classification, the primary criterion is cell structure. Reason (R) is true because blue-green algae are prokaryotes. They have a primitive cellular organization lacking a well-defined nucleus and membrane-bound cell organelles.

Therefore, (A) is false but (R) is true.

Answer: (A) is false but (R) is true.

Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R).

Assertion (A): In R.H. Whittaker's classification, fungi were separated from plants and placed in a distinct kingdom, unlike in the earlier two-kingdom system.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:
options: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of Assertion (A)
Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true but Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of Assertion (A)
Assertion (A) is true but Reason (R) is false
Assertion (A) is false but Reason (R) is true
questions.solution:
Assertion (A) is true because the earlier two-kingdom system grouped fungi with plants since both possessed a cell wall, but R.H. Whittaker placed them in a separate Kingdom Fungi.

Fungi are heterotrophic with chitinous cell walls, which fundamentally distinguishes them from autotrophic plants that have cellulosic cell walls.

Therefore, both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true, and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of Assertion (A).

Answer: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of Assertion (A)

questions.q: In a biogas plant, certain bacteria are utilized for the production of methane gas from cattle dung. Identify the broad taxonomic group to which these bacteria belong, and another natural habitat where they are commonly found.
questions.solution:
The bacteria responsible for the production of methane (biogas) from cattle dung are methanogens.

Answer: Archaebacteria and Marshy areas

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q:
Read the following statements regarding the sexual cycle in fungi:

A. In Ascomycetes, karyogamy and meiosis take place in the ascus.
B. In Basidiomycetes, plasmogamy occurs by the fusion of two vegetative or somatic cells.
C. In Phycomycetes, a distinct dikaryophase occurs before zygospore formation.
D. Fungi form fruiting bodies in which reduction division occurs.

How many of the above statements are correct?
questions.solution:
Statement A is correct: In Ascomycetes, the fusion of nuclei (karyogamy) and subsequent reduction division (meiosis) occur within sac-like structures called asci.

Statement B is correct: Basidiomycetes lack distinct sex organs, and plasmogamy is achieved through the fusion of two vegetative or somatic cells of different strains or genotypes.

Statement C is incorrect: In Phycomycetes, the fusion of two gametes (plasmogamy) is immediately followed by karyogamy, resulting in a diploid zygote or zygospore. They do not exhibit an intervening dikaryophase.

Statement D is correct: In higher fungi, after the dikaryotic stage, parental nuclei fuse to become diploid. The fungi form fruiting bodies in which meiosis (reduction division) occurs, leading to the formation of haploid spores.

Therefore, three statements (A, B, and D) are correct.

Answer: Three

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q:
Read the following statements regarding the characteristics of kingdoms in Whittaker's five-kingdom classification:
I. Kingdom Monera: Prokaryotic cell type, non-cellulosic cell wall, and cellular body organisation.
II. Kingdom Protista: Eukaryotic cell type, cell wall absent in all members, and cellular body organisation.
III. Kingdom Fungi: Eukaryotic cell type, chitinous cell wall, and tissue/organ system body organisation.
IV. Kingdom Plantae: Eukaryotic cell type, cellulosic cell wall, and tissue/organ body organisation.
V. Kingdom Animalia: Eukaryotic cell type, cell wall absent, and tissue/organ/organ system body organisation.

How many of the above statements are correct?
questions.solution:
According to Whittaker's five-kingdom classification:

Statement I is correct: Monera are prokaryotes with a non-cellulosic cell wall and cellular body organisation.

Statement II is incorrect: Protists are eukaryotes with a cellular body organisation, but a cell wall is present in some members (not absent in all).

Statement III is incorrect: Fungi are eukaryotes with a chitinous cell wall, but their body organisation is multicellular/loose tissue, not tissue/organ system.

Statement IV is correct: Plantae are eukaryotes with a cellulosic cell wall and tissue/organ body organisation.

Statement V is correct: Animalia are eukaryotes without a cell wall and possess tissue/organ/organ system body organisation.

Therefore, exactly three statements (I, IV, and V) are correct.

Answer: Three

questions.solution:
Deuteromycetes are commonly known as imperfect fungi because only their asexual or vegetative phases are known. When the sexual forms of these fungi are discovered, they are often moved to Ascomycetes or Basidiomycetes.

Alternaria and Trichoderma are classic examples of Deuteromycetes, making the Assertion (A) true.

The Reason (R) correctly states the defining characteristic of this group (the absence of a known sexual phase), which is exactly why they are termed 'imperfect'. Thus, both (A) and (R) are true, and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).

Answer: Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: An organism is observed to be unicellular and lacks a nuclear membrane. Further analysis reveals that it completely lacks a cell wall and is among the smallest known living cells. Which of the following groups does this organism belong to?
questions.solution:
The absence of a nuclear membrane indicates that the organism is a prokaryote, which eliminates slime moulds as they are eukaryotic protists.

Among prokaryotes, Mycoplasma are unique because they completely lack a cell wall. They are also recognized as the smallest living cells known.

Archaebacteria and cyanobacteria are prokaryotes, but they both possess a cell wall. Therefore, the described organism belongs to Mycoplasma.

Answer: Mycoplasma

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: In some fungi, the fusion of two haploid cells does not immediately result in a diploid cell (2n). Instead, an intervening dikaryotic stage (n + n) occurs before the nuclei fuse. Which of the following pairs of fungal classes distinctly exhibits this prolonged dikaryophase?
questions.solution:
In certain fungi, the fusion of two haploid cells immediately results in diploid cells (2n), which is characteristic of lower fungi like Phycomycetes.

However, according to NCERT, in Ascomycetes and Basidiomycetes, plasmogamy is not immediately followed by karyogamy. This creates an intervening dikaryotic stage (n + n, i.e., two nuclei per cell) known as a dikaryon, and the phase is called the dikaryophase.

Deuteromycetes are known as imperfect fungi because only their asexual or vegetative phases are known, and a sexual cycle is not observed in them.

Thus, the distinct dikaryophase is exhibited by Ascomycetes and Basidiomycetes.

Answer: Ascomycetes and Basidiomycetes

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: In R.H. Whittaker's Five Kingdom Classification, fungi were removed from the plant kingdom and placed in a distinct kingdom of their own. Which of the following pairs of main criteria primarily justified this separation?
options: Cell structure and Mode of nutrition
Mode of nutrition and Phylogenetic relationships
questions.solution:
Earlier classification systems placed fungi and green plants together despite fundamental differences. When Whittaker's criteria were applied, fungi were separated into Kingdom Fungi primarily due to two major differences:
1. Mode of nutrition: Fungi are heterotrophic, whereas green plants are autotrophic.
2. Cell structure: Fungi possess a chitinous cell wall, whereas green plants have a cellulosic cell wall.

Body organisation is not the primary distinguishing factor here, as both groups largely consist of multicellular or tissue-level organisms. Thus, cell structure and mode of nutrition were the primary criteria justifying their separation.

Answer: Cell structure and Mode of nutrition

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q:
Arrange the following events in the correct chronological sequence during the sexual reproduction of a basidiomycete :
A. Karyogamy
B. Meiosis in zygote
C. Plasmogamy
D. Formation of dikaryon (n + n)

Choose the correct sequence from the options given below :
questions.solution:
The sexual cycle in fungi like basidiomycetes begins with plasmogamy (C), which is the fusion of protoplasms of two compatible haploid hyphae.

In basidiomycetes, plasmogamy is not immediately followed by the fusion of nuclei. This delay results in an intervening dikaryotic stage where each cell has two nuclei, known as the formation of a dikaryon (n + n) (D).

Later, the two nuclei fuse, an event called karyogamy (A), resulting in a diploid zygote.

Finally, the diploid zygote undergoes reduction division, or meiosis (B), to produce haploid spores.

Therefore, the correct chronological sequence is C $\rightarrow$ D $\rightarrow$ A $\rightarrow$ B.

Answer: C $\rightarrow$ D $\rightarrow$ A $\rightarrow$ B

Read the following list of organisms:
Anabaena, Saccharomyces, Rhizobium, Gonyaulax, Trichoderma, Thermus aquaticus

How many of the given organisms are prokaryotic and belong to Kingdom Monera?
questions.solution:
Organisms belonging to Kingdom Monera are prokaryotes. They lack a true nucleus and membrane-bound organelles.

1. Anabaena is a cyanobacterium (blue-green alga) and belongs to Kingdom Monera.
2. Saccharomyces (yeast) is a unicellular eukaryote belonging to Kingdom Fungi.
3. Rhizobium is a symbiotic nitrogen-fixing bacterium, placed in Kingdom Monera.
4. Gonyaulax is a dinoflagellate, which is a unicellular eukaryote placed in Kingdom Protista.
5. Trichoderma is a fungus, hence eukaryotic.
6. Thermus aquaticus is a bacterium, hence prokaryotic and belongs to Kingdom Monera.

Therefore, there are three prokaryotic organisms in the given list: Anabaena, Rhizobium, and Thermus aquaticus.

Answer: Three

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Keystone species deserve protection because these
options: are capable of surviving in harsh environmental conditions
indicate presence of certain minerals in the soil
have become rare due to overexploitation
play an important role in supporting other species.
questions.solution: Keystone species are species which have significant and disproportionately large influence on the community. Removal or decrease in their number causes disruption in structure and function of community. For example in intertidal regions starfish feeds on mussels. Removal of starfish leads to dominance of mussels that excludes algae and browsing species. In tropical rain forests, fig trees function as keystone species as they provide fruits to a number of animals during the period of food scarcity.

questions.solution: Rudolf Virchow was the first to suggest that new cells are formed from the division of the preexisting cells - omnis-cellula-e-cellula (every cell is derived from a previous cell). Robert Hooke was the first to coin the term "cell" for small structures in a piece of cork under a microscope. His observations were published in a book named micrographia. Leeuwenhoek was the first person to observe and describe microscopic organisms and living cell. He observed nucleus in RBC of salmon fish and used simple lens and observed nuclei and unicellular organisms including bacteria. In 1676, he described the bacteria and gave the term animalcules. His observations laid the foundations for the science of bacteriology and microbiology. Robert Brown (1831) described and named nucleus.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: "Ordines Anomali" of Bentham and Hooker includes
options: seed plants showing abnormal forms of growth and development
plants described only in fossil state
plants described in the literature but which Bentham and Hooker did not see in original
a few orders which could not be placed satisfactorily in the classification.
questions.solution: The system of classification of seed plants presented by Bentham and Hooker, represented the most well developed classification of natural system. The classification was published in 3 volumes of 'Genera plantarum'. The system divided phanerogams or seed plants into 3 classes dicotyledons, gymnospermae and monocotyledons. Dicotyledons were further subdivided into 3 subclasses - polypetalae, gamopetalae and monochlamydae based on the presence or absence of petals and their fusion. They were further divided into series, orders and families. No orders were recognised within monochlamydae and monocotyledons, the series being directly divided into families. But the system had a lot of demerits within it. He did not know the affinities of the families placed under 'Ordines anomate' and the families were tentativily grouped together. So, a few orders were not placed satisfactorily in the classification. Monochlamydae is an unnatural assemblage of taxa, which belongs elsewhere. The creation of this group has resulted in the separation of many closely related families.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: The bacteria Pseudomonas aeruginosa is useful because of its ability to
options: transfer genes from one plant to another
decompose a variety of organic compounds
fix atmospheric nitrogen in the soil
produce a wide variety of antibiotics.
questions.solution:
Pseudomonas aeruginosa is a Gram-negative, aerobic rod belonging to the bacterial family Pseudomonadaceae. These bacteria are common inhabitants of soil water. They occur regularly on the surfaces of plants and occassionally on the surfaces of animals.
The bacterium will grow in the absence of $\mathrm{O}_2$ if $\mathrm{NO}_3$ is available as a respiratory electron acceptor. $Q, a$ possesses the metabolic versatility. Organic growth factors are not required, and it can use more than thirty organic compounds for growth. Pseudomonas aeruginosa is often observed growing in "distilled water" which is evidence of its minimal nutritional requirements.
- It is able to grow at temperatures as high as 42 degrees.
- Its tolerance to a wide variety of physical conditions, including temperature, contributes to its ecological success and makes it suitable for decomposing a variety of organic compounds in varied environmental conditions.

options: makes the food easy to digest
questions.solution: Spirulina is a blue-green algae. Spirulina platensis is one of the richest source of protein, containing 40-50 percent crude protein on dry weight basis which under favourable condition may reach upto 70 percent. Its protein has balanced composition containing all essential amino-acids and lysine and tryptophan being present in sufficient quantities. Spirulina is also rich in vitamins, particularly Vit. $\mathrm{B}_{12}$, which is not common in plant products and contains considerable amounts of fats, carbohydrates and minerals. It's lipids are made up of unsaturated fatty acids that do not form cholesterol.

questions.q: Which one of the following is linked to the discovery of bordeaux mixture as a popular fungicide?
questions.solution:
Bordeaux mixture was discovered by Millardet in France in 1882. It is prepared by dissolving 40 g of copper sulphate and 40 g of calcium hydroxide in 5 L of water. It was first used to control downy mildew disease of grape-vine that is caused by a fungus Plasmopara viticola.
Black rust of wheat is caused by Puccinia graminis tritici. The use of fungicide dithane Z-78 and dithane M-45 control the disease even at lower concentration.
Loose smut of wheat is caused by Ustilago tritici. The use of fungicides (systemic fungicide like D-785 and F-461) give quite encouraging result.

questions.solution: When bacteriophage infects a bacterium, it entirely depends on the host for its multiplication. It utilises the host machinery for replication and produce a large number of progeny phage particles. This cycle is known as lytic cycle.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: In Whittaker's system of classification, prokaryotes belong to the kingdom
questions.solution: RH Whittaker (1969) proposed a Five Kingdom Classification. The kingdoms defined by him were named-Monera, Protista, Fungi, Plantae and Animalia. The main criteria for classification used by him include cell structure, thallus organisation, mode of nutrition, reproduction and phylogenetic relationships. All the prokaryotic organisms were grouped together under kingdom-Monera and unicellular eukaryotic organisms were placed in kingdom Protista. The fungi were placed is a separated kingdom, ie, kingdom-Fungi. The kingdom-Plantae and Animalia, commonly referred to as plant and animal kingdoms, respectively.

questions.q: There exists a close association between the alga and the fungus within a lichen. The fungus
options: fixes the atmospheric nitrogen for the alga
provides protection, anchorage and absorption for the alga
questions.solution: Lichen is a symbiotic association between a fungus and an algae (green alga or blue green alga). The algal partner of lichen is called as phycobiont while fungal partner is termed as mycobiont. Lichen develops into a unique morphological form which is quite distinct from either partner. The fungal partner of lichen helps in the absorption of water and mineral to algal partner additionally it also provides protection and anchorage to algal partner of lichen. In exchange of this, the fungal partner absorbs prepared food material from algal partner. This food material is prepared by the algal partner of lichen through the process of photosynthesis.

questions.solution: Noctiluca is a marine and pelagic dinoflagellate which shows bio-lumine scence. At night, it produces the effect of burning of sea. The luminescence is caused by a bio-luminescent luciferin, which under the influence of an enzymeluciferase emits light.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q:
Protists are
(i) unicellular and prokaryote
(ii) unicellular and eukaryote
(iii) multicellular and eukaryote
(iv) autotroph or heterotroph
questions.solution: A five kingdom division of organisms was proposed by Whittaker. Protista is one of that division. It is a kingdom of unicellular, eukaryotic organism. Many of them are photosynthetic autotrophs, unicellular algae and diatoms. Some protists are heterotrophic, e.g. Protozoa.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Which are sensitive to $\mathrm{SO}_2$ pollution?
questions.solution: Lichens are sensitive to $\mathrm{SO}_2$ environment. They can not grow in sulphur dioxide pollutated area. So, lichens are called pollution indicating plants.

questions.q: Among plants "pheromones" are secreted by the cells of the following plants for given function
options: all plants for growth and development
questions.solution: Pheromone is a substance secreted to outside by an indivisual and received by a second indivisual of the same specic in which it induce a specific reaction e.g. fusion of two yeast cells during sexual reproduction.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: 'Reindeer moss' is common name for
questions.solution: The bitter substance present in lichens are removed before being used as fodder. Lichens form favourite food for reindeers, cattles etc. Cladonia rangifera is the commonly used food for reindeer in tundra regions.
